full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury J: By this application the plaintiff petitioner Khorashani Oil Refinery Mills Ltd. seeks for direction from this court upon the defendants to deliver 1361. 184 M.T. of crude degummed Soyabean oil (C.D.S.0) stored in the tank terminal of International Tank Terminal (defendant No. 7) on furnishing indemnity bond in favour of the defendant. 

 3. The plaintiff petitioner's case is that it entered into a contract with Devon Industries Sdn. Bhd. of Singapore for supply of 1369 M.T. of Crude Degummed Soyabean Oil (C.D.S.O.) in bulk C & F. free out Chittagong by shipment from any South American Port. The Shipment date was to be not later than 31.7.93. The plaintiff petitioner opened a Letter of Credit No. IMAM/BSF/DLR/131/93 dated 20.5.93 in favour of the said supplier Devon Industries for U.S. $ 5,98,253. The plaintiff banker, Janata Bank (Proforma defendant No. 12) opened the aforesaid Irrevocable Letter of Credit in favour of the supplier through the advising bank namely, Standard Chartered Bank, Singapore. The plaintiff come to learn that the supplier had entered into voyage charter party with the owner of defendant No. 1 M.P. DOLORES through defendant No. 4 acting through defendant No.8. The defendant No.8 Ocean Wine Freight Dookers Pte Ltd of Singapore in turn issued the Bill of Lading in respect of the plaintiff petitioner cargo. It was confirmed by the telex that the bills of lading were in order. The plaintiff petitioner's bank, proforma defendant No 12 was informed by the advising bank by telex that it had negotiated the documents for U.S. $ 5,98,253 under the said letter of credit issued by pro-defendant No.12 and had certified that all the terms and conditions of the credit had been complied with. The defendant No. 6 being the agent of defendant nos. 1.2 and by letter dated 20th June, 1993 informed the plaintiff petitioner that the defendant No. 1 i.e. the Tank Vessel M.T. DOLORES was expected to arrive at Chittagong Port on or about 25.6.93 and the vessel would take berth at River Mooring (C.D.S.O. berth) to discharging cargo and requested the plaintiff petitioner to enter and make necessary arrangement in all respect to receive and store the plaintiff cargo on arrival/ berthing at the River Mooring and further requested to advise the name of the nominated tank terminal in which the plaintiff petitioner intends to store the said cargo. The survey in respect of the quantity of cargo belonging to the plaintiff petitioner was carried out by Cargo Control Bangladesh PTE Ltd. and Superintendent (Bangladesh) service for the plaintiff and the survey Certificate relating to the plaintiff petitioner's cargo and consignment of other consigns in Bangladesh was signed by the said supplier and their authorised officer on 29.6,93. Thereafter the plaintiff petitioner's cargo to the quantum of 1369 MT was stored at the Tank Terminal of the defendant No.7 at Chittagong Port. Thereafter the plaintiff called upon the defendant no. 6 by its letter dated 24.7.93 and requested him to issue a delivery order to enable the plaintiff to take delivery from the tank terminal of the cargo. But the defendant No.6 in reply to the letter of the plaintiff petitioner wrote to the plaintiff by his letter dated 26th July 1993 that they were sorry and regret to advise that they had been instructed by the owner/carriers not to issue the delivery order for the entire cargo of 9500 M.T. of C.D.S.O. discharged into Customs bonded tank at Chittagong untill/unless the original bills of lading as issued at load ports were surrendered by the Charterers/Suppliers (Devon) to the owners. Hence this application for direction on the defendants to delivery of 1369 MT. of C.D.S.O. Stored in the tank terminal of proforma defendant No.7 to the plaintiff petitioner 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-4 have opposed the application interalia on he ground that the owner of the Vessel neither signed any charter party agreement nor authorised Ocean wide freight Brokers (Pvt.) Ltd. defendant No.8 to sign the alleged charter party agreement and further the said defendant by telex dated 11.8.93 informed the owners of the vessel that they had not signed the charter party agreement on 28.4.93 nor any of their authorised officers signed the same and accordingly the said charter party is fraudulent and the defendants were not bound by the same. It is further said there were many claimants for the cargo who have commenced legal proceeding claimed title to the cargo and the owners of the vessel are responsible to deliver the cargo only to the original person or none else. The defendants under law are required to deliver the cargo only to consignee who furnished original bills of lading issued at the load port and since the plaintiff petitioner failed to furnish load port bills of lading they were not entitled to an order for direction for delivery of the cargo to them. 

 5. Mr. Khan saifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner interalia submitted that suppliers had entered into a charter party agreement with the owners of the vessel Tromoy Shipping of Arendal Norway (defendant No.4) through their agent Ocean wide Freight Brokers Pte. Ltd. (defendant No. 8) and thus the defendant No. 8 were authorised to issue bills of lading at Singapore and it was not necessary to furnish original bills of lading issued at the load port. He has further submitted that the plaintiff petitioner had received invoice from the supplier Devon and had opened letter of credit in favour of the supplier through their Banker proforma defendant No. 12 and had paid full value of the cargo and its freight. The bills of lading were issued by defendant No.8 on the basis of the charter party agreement dated 28.4.93 entered into by Devon Industries Singapore with the agents and owner of the vessel. The authority given to defendant No. 8 to issue the bills of lading the acceptance of the bills of lading by the defendant No.6 agents for defendants 1, 2 and 4 the import manifest and the quantification survey made by the plaintiff and the unloading of the cargo at the nominated tanker of the plaintiff petitioner establish the title of the plaintiff petitioner over the cargo discharge and stored in the tanker. The consignment of the plaintiff now stored in the tank terminal is not the subject matter of any admiralty suit or other proceedings in any court and the petitioners claimed its own cargo in the instant suit for refusal of defendant opposite party No.1 to issue any delivery order on flimsy ground. They are therefore, entitled to take delivery of the same. These facts have not been seriously challenged by the defendant except the authority under which the bills of Lading were issued from Singapore and their agents. 

 6. Keeping these facts in mind, I also note that the consignment arrived at the Chittagong port 7 months ago and the cargo is perishable item and unless it is cleared from the tanker the entire cargo Worth several cores of take may become unfit for human consumption . It is nobody's interest that the consignment of such high price should be allowed to perish, and this fact cannot be ignored by this court. I also find that the consignment which was imported by the plaintiff petitioner was initially discharged on the basis of bills of lading issued from Singapore. The defendant had requested the plaintiff petitioner to take delivery of his consignment. Accordingly the plaintiff petitioner had the consignment surveyed with regard to its quantification and an import manifest was also issued. The consignment of the plaintiff petitioner has also been stored with defendant No.7 International Tank Terminal who are the nominated tanker of the plaintiff petitioner. 

 7. In these facts and circumstances, the plaintiff petitioner have at least out a prima facie case in respect of their claim to the consignment, although the matter of the validity of the bills of lading issued from Singapore is to be decided in the suit itself. The defendant Nos. 1-4 s have made a counter claim against the plaintiff. In these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that the plaintiff petitioner is entitled to certificate from the vessel M.T. DOLORES on his agent for delivery of the cargo but subject to a security in the form of indemnity bond to cover the costs of the cargo, damages and dead freight claimed by the defendants. 

 8. Accordingly, I allow this application and direct the Master of the vessel or his agent to issue delivery certificate for 1369 M.T. of crude degummed Soyabean Oil in favour of the plaintiff petitioner subject to the furnishing of a satisfactory indemnity bond for U.S. $ 22,91,153 being the value of the consignment and claimed for damages, dead freight etc. to this Court in favour of defendant Nos. 1-4 by the plaintiff and the furnishing of original bills of lading issued by defendant No. 8 to the master of the vessel.
